title: Financial Services Compensation Scheme of Last Resort Levy (Collection) Bill 2021
short_title: Financial Services Compensation Scheme of Last Resort Levy (Collection) Bill 2021

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would administer collection of industry levies supporting the financial services compensation scheme of last resort, including calculation estimates, payment notices and enforcement.
The Australian Securities and Investments Commission would collect levies, require supporting information and issue notices giving firms at least 30 days to pay.
It would commence with the companion levy bill, with reasonable excuse and reasonable steps protections applying to specified information offences and shortfall penalties.
changes: Late levy payments could attract interest at 20 per cent a year, calculated monthly, unless an extension applied.
False or misleading statements causing an entity's own levy shortfall could attract a penalty twice the shortfall.
The regulator could waive levies or penalties where exceptional circumstances justified doing so.
Failure to supply or substantiate required information would be a strict liability offence carrying a maximum of 10 penalty units.
summary.affected: Financial firms liable for scheme levies and the scheme operator would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Alan Tudge
speeches.brief: The Financial Services Compensation Scheme of Last Resort Levy (Collection) Bill 2021 establishes a levy framework to fund the Compensation Scheme of Last Resort, comprising an annual levy collected from January 2023 and a one-off levy in 2022-23. It gives ASIC responsibility for issuing levy notices, collecting payments, seeking information, and imposing penalties for late payment or incorrect information.
